name: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
problem: Attention's softmax makes training non-parallelisable across the sequence and gives O(L) KV cache at inference; the paper wanted both Transformer training parallelism and O(1)-state inference without giving up quality.
mechanism: Proposes retention, a sequence model with three equivalent computation paradigms: parallel (for training), recurrent (for O(1)-memory inference) and chunkwise recurrent (a numerically stable training form). The recurrence is a fixed-decay exponential: S_n = gamma * S_{n-1} + K_n^T V_n with gamma = alpha^{1/L} a learned per-head decay, so the implicit attention weight between positions i and j is alpha^{(i-j)/L}, a deterministic geometric decay with no softmax and no data-dependent denominator. Three retention modes are used in parallel with different decay rates (a 1x1, a 1/4, and a 1/16 rate), the fastest decay on the highest-resolution stream, plus a GroupNorm-style normalisation, and Grouped-Retention or MSR (multi-scale retention) with a GroupNorm-based normalisation replacing softmax denominator. State is a fixed-size (d_model, d_head) matrix per head, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is no KV cache and decode memory does not grow with context.
speedup_reported: Claims 7x faster training, 5x faster inference and 4x lower inference memory versus a standard Transformer of equivalent modelling power, plus parallelizable scaling to 128K context. Hardware was A100-class. These are the authors' own numbers on their own implementation and scale-law comparison; the 7x/5x/4x triple did not reproduce in production. RetNet did not become a shipped architecture in any mainstream engine: no retnet entry in llama.cpp's arch registry and no native row in the vLLM supported-models list.
notes: arXiv preprint; no peer-reviewed venue on the abs page. Theoretically clean and the explicit O(1)-state claim is genuinely correct, but fixed-decay retention is a weaker retrieval mechanism than data-dependent gating: it cannot decide to look back past the decay horizon, which is the same weakness the 'Based' paper (arXiv 2402.18668) measured directly. Model weights were never released, so adoption is impossible regardless of the paper's claims. Filed under attention rather than ssm because it is a replacement-for-attention mechanism, not an SSM in the Mamba line.
